mainTopic: מעילה in disqualified קדשי קדשים: שעת היתר לכהנים and why each case of the משנה is needed
overview: The first משנה of מסכת מעילה asks whether מעילה (misusing holy property) still applies to קדשי קדשים that became פסול. It lists cases where the offering was ruined before it could be eaten: slaughter or collection of the blood in the south, slaughter or sprinkling at night, and slaughter with the intent חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו. In all of these, מעילה still applies. רבי יהושע then gives the rule: if the offering ever had a שעת היתר לכהנים, there is no more מעילה, and if it never did, מעילה stays. The משנה gives examples of each side, such as meat left overnight, meat that became טמא, or blood handled by unfit people. The גמרא first asks why the south case even needs saying. It answers that we might have compared it to קדשים שמתו, but the south is a valid place for קדשים קלים, so the slaughter is still real. Next, the גמרא explains why every place and time case in the משנה is needed. Finally, it asks what wrong-intent offerings are still fit for, and answers that the blood service still takes effect on them by making them פיגול.

steps.title: Most-holy offerings slaughtered in the wrong place still carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a basic case. If קדשי קדשים were slaughtered in the south of the עזרה instead of the north, a person who benefits from them is still guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Most-holy offerings that were slaughtered in the south: one is liable for misusing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that a most-holy offering ruined by being slaughtered in the wrong place still belongs to הקדש. Anyone who benefits from it commits מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the north, so slaughtering them in the south makes them פסול. You might think a ruined offering loses its holiness. The משנה says it does not: the animal never became permitted to anyone, so it still belongs to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: The most-holy class of offerings (like עולה, חטאת, אשם), which must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה
One is liable for מעילה: benefiting from holy property. The person brings a קרבן אשם and pays the value plus an extra fifth.
South: the wrong side of the עזרה for slaughtering קדשי קדשים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that 'disqualified' means 'no longer holy.' A פסול offering can still be fully הקדש, and that is exactly why מעילה applies here.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole משנה. Being פסול does not by itself remove מעילה. What matters, as רבי יהושע will explain, is whether the offering was ever permitted to the כהנים.

phrases.english: Most-holy offerings that one slaughtered in the south
phrases.notes: These offerings belong in the north of the courtyard, so the south makes them invalid.

phrases.english: one is liable for misusing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קדשי קדשים ששחטן בדרום מועלין בהן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south are פסול, but מעילה still applies to them.

steps.title: Mixed-up place and time cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds more cases where the offering was ruined. Either the slaughter or the collecting of the blood was done on the wrong side. Or the slaughter or the sprinkling was done at night instead of by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered in the south and collected the blood in the north, or slaughtered in the north and collected the blood in the south; if he slaughtered by day and sprinkled at night, or slaughtered at night and sprinkled by day...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more ways the offering can be ruined before it is ever eaten. The ruling for these cases comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here only one part of the service was done wrong, while the other part was done right. Even so, one wrong step ruins the offering, so it never becomes permitted to the כהנים. Switching place (north and south) is matched by switching time (day and night).

keyTerms.meaning: He collected their blood in a vessel. This is one of the main steps of the service.
North: the correct side of the עזרה for slaughtering קדשי קדשים and collecting their blood
He sprinkled the blood on the מזבח. This is the step that makes the meat permitted.
Night: an invalid time for the service of קרבנות

phrases.english: If he slaughtered them in the south and collected their blood in the north,
or in the north and collected their blood in the south,
phrases.notes: The word 'slaughtered' is left out here but understood: he slaughtered in the north.

phrases.english: if he slaughtered by day and sprinkled at night,
or at night and sprinkled by day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases of disqualification that will share the same ruling as step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistake of place or time in any single step of the service ruins the offering. The ruling of מעילה is given in step 3.

steps.title: Bad intent during slaughter also keeps מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The last case is slaughtering with the intent to eat or sprinkle outside the proper time (פיגול) or outside the proper place. In this case, and in all the cases listed before it, מעילה applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if he slaughtered them with intent beyond their time or outside their place: one is liable for misusing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the case of a wrong thought during slaughter. Then it gives the ruling, מועלין בהן, for this case and for all the cases in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here nothing was physically done wrong. The person only had a wrong intention while slaughtering, and that alone ruins the offering. Since the offering never became permitted, it still belongs to הקדש, just like in the other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond its time: the intent to eat the meat or sprinkle the blood after the allowed time. This makes the offering פִּגּוּל.
An offering ruined by the intent, during the service, to eat it past its allowed time
Outside its place: the intent to eat the meat or sprinkle the blood outside the proper area. This also makes the offering פסול.

steps.confusionAlert: חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו here are about what he intended while slaughtering. They do not mean he actually slaughtered late or in another place.
steps.whatToRemember: Wrong place, wrong time, or wrong intent: in every case where the offering was ruined before it could be eaten, מעילה still applies.

phrases.english: or if he slaughtered them beyond its time
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering with the plan to eat or sprinkle it after its allowed time.

phrases.english: or outside its place
one is liable for misusing them.
phrases.notes: This ruling covers all the cases listed since the start of step 2, not just this last one.

steps.triggerLanguage: או ששחטן חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו מועלין בהן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of cases and gives the ruling for all of them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all these cases of disqualification, including פיגול and intent outside its place, מעילה applies.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's general rule: was it ever permitted to the כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives a general principle. If an offering ever had a moment when the כהנים were allowed to eat it, there is no more מעילה. If it never had such a moment, מעילה applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stated a rule: any offering that had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים, one is not liable for misusing it. Any offering that never had a time when it was permitted to the כהנים, one is liable for misusing it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע explains the reason behind all the cases so far, using one simple test: was this offering ever permitted to the כהנים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה applies to things that belong only to ה׳. Once the blood was properly sprinkled and the כהנים were allowed to eat the meat, it no longer has that status, so there is no מעילה even if it is ruined later. All the earlier cases were ruined before that point, which is why מעילה applied.

keyTerms.meaning: A general principle that sums up many cases
A time when it was permitted: a moment when the offering was fit to be eaten by the כהנים
One is not liable for מעילה

steps.confusionAlert: שעת היתר does not mean a moment before the offering was ruined. It means the whole service was done properly, the blood was sprinkled, and the meat was actually permitted to be eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to the whole perek. Whether מעילה applies depends on whether the offering ever became permitted, not on whether it is פסול now.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: any offering that had a time of permission for the priests
one is not liable for misusing it,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים –
phrases.english: and any offering that did not have a time of permission for the priests
one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the principle that explains all the cases in steps 1 to 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If an offering had a שעת היתר לכהנים, there is no מעילה. If it never had one, there is מעילה.

steps.title: Which offering counts as once permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for examples of an offering that had a שעת היתר but was later ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the offering that had a time of permission for the כהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a clarifying question to show what the other side of רבי יהושע's rule looks like. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have only seen cases where מעילה applies. Now the משנה wants to show cases where the offering was valid at first and was ruined only afterward, so מעילה no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one is it? A standard way the משנה asks for an example

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים?
phrases.english: Which is the one that had a time of permission for the priests?

steps.triggerLanguage: איזו היא שהיה לה שעת היתר לכהנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for examples of the first half of רבי יהושע's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Concrete examples of an offering that was once permitted to the כהנים and was ruined afterward

steps.title: Left overnight, became impure, or went out
steps.stepSummary: The answer gives three cases. The meat was left overnight (נותר), it became טמא, or it left its proper area. Each of these happened after the meat was already permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: One that was left overnight, one that became impure, and one that went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names three ways an offering can be ruined after it was already permitted to the כהנים. In these cases there is no מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three problems happen only after the blood was sprinkled and the meat became fit to eat. Since there was a שעת היתר, the meat left the category of 'belonging only to ה׳,' and a later problem does not bring that status back.

keyTerms.meaning: That stayed overnight: meat left past its time to be eaten, which becomes נוֹתָר
It became טמא (ritually impure)
That went out of its proper area (the עזרה for קדשי קדשים) and became פסול

steps.whatToRemember: Ruined before it was permitted means מעילה still applies (steps 1 to 3). Ruined after it was permitted, as with לינה, טומאה, or יציאה, means no מעילה.

phrases.english: One that remained overnight, and one that became impure, and one that went out.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לינה, טומאה, and יציאה are problems that come after the meat was permitted, so there is no מעילה.

steps.title: Which offering never had a time of permission?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for examples of the opposite case: an offering that never had a שעת היתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which offering never had a time when the כהנים were allowed to eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks about the other side of רבי יהושע's rule: an offering that was never permitted to the כהנים. This question sets up the list of cases in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked for examples of offerings that were permitted and only later ruined. Now the משנה asks for offerings that were ruined before they were ever permitted. According to רבי יהושע, these still carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And which is it? This is a formula that asks for examples.
A moment of permission, when the meat was allowed to be eaten
The priests, who eat the meat of many offerings

phrases.english: And which is the one that did not have
a time of permission for the priests?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question in step 5, but now for the opposite category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Examples of an offering that was never permitted to the כהנים

steps.title: Cases ruined before ever being permitted
steps.stepSummary: Three cases: slaughter with intent outside the proper time, slaughter with intent outside the proper place, and blood collected and sprinkled by unfit people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is one that was slaughtered with intent to eat or sprinkle outside its time, or outside its place, or whose blood unfit people collected and sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question with three cases. In each one, the offering was ruined before the blood was properly sprinkled, so the meat was never permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat becomes permitted to the כהנים only after its blood is properly sprinkled. In all three cases the problem happened before or during the blood service, so a permitted moment never came. That is why מעילה stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent to eat or sprinkle beyond the allowed time. This is פִּגּוּל.
Intent to eat or sprinkle outside the proper area
People unfit for Temple service
Collecting the blood in a vessel
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Ruined before the meat was permitted: מעילה applies. Ruined after the meat was permitted: no more מעילה.

phrases.english: One that was slaughtered [with intent] beyond its time,
outside its place,
and one whose blood unfit people collected
and sprinkled its blood.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פיגול, intent outside the proper place, and blood collected and sprinkled by unfit people

steps.title: Why say south-slaughtered offerings carry מעילה? Isn't it obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's first case and asks why it needed to be taught at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches that if קדשי קדשים were slaughtered in the south, מעילה applies. But that is obvious! Just because they were slaughtered in the wrong spot, should they lose their מעילה status?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה's opening case. It then challenges it: this ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is still holy property even if it was slaughtered in the wrong spot. A mistake in the service should not make it less holy, so there seems to be no reason to think מעילה would stop. The גמרא wants to know what the משנה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Offerings of the most sacred level, which must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה
The south side of the Temple courtyard
It is obvious! The גמרא asks why something needed to be said.
Misusing holy property for personal benefit

phrases.english: GEMARA
It teaches: offerings of the most sacred order
that one slaughtered in the south: one is liable for misusing them.
It is obvious!
Just because their slaughter was in the south,
should we take them out of the status of misuse?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן בַּדָּרוֹם – מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן. פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended. The גמרא now turns back to the משנה's first case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's ruling about slaughter in the south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mistake in the service should not take away the animal's holy status, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One might have compared it to an animal that died
steps.stepSummary: It was needed, because one could think that improper slaughter in the south is like strangling the animal. That would be like קדשים שמתו, which lose מעילה by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought this: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן that sacrificial animals that died leave מעילה by Torah law. So too, slaughtering קדשי קדשים in the south is like strangling them, and they would lose מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is not obvious. It explains the mistaken idea the משנה wants to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן rules that a holy animal that died on its own is no longer subject to מעילה by Torah law. Slaughter in the wrong place for קדשי קדשים might count as no slaughter at all, like killing the animal by strangling. Then the animal would be treated as one that died and would lose מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed. This means the ruling is not obvious.
It could enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought.
Sacrificial animals that died without proper slaughter
By Torah law
We strangled them, meaning they were killed improperly

phrases.english: It was necessary,
since it could enter your mind to say

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that since Ulla said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Sacrificial animals that died
have left the status of misuse by Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לְגַבֵּי דָרוֹם,
phrases.english: so too, offerings of the most sacred order, with regard to the south,
are as if we had strangled them.
phrases.notes: He means slaughter in the wrong spot might not count as real slaughter at all, just like killing the animal any other way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 9 by showing a reasonable mistaken view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed to block a mistaken comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughter of קדשי קדשים in the south is like strangling, so the animal counts like קדשים שמתו and loses מעילה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the conclusion. It is the mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the משנה is coming to reject.

steps.title: South slaughter is still real slaughter, unlike an animal that died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that an animal that died is fit for nothing. The south, however, is a valid place to slaughter קדשים קלים, so slaughter there is still real slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: animals that died are not fit at all. But the south, even though it is not the right place for קדשי קדשים, is the right place for קדשים קלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the lesson of the משנה and rejects the comparison to an animal that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that died has no valid act of slaughter at all. Slaughtering in the south is a real, valid kind of sacrificial slaughter, because קדשים קלים may be slaughtered there. So it is a flawed sacrificial slaughter, not a 'strangling,' and the animal keeps its מעילה status.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us. This introduces the real lesson.
They are not fit at all
Granted that. This admits a point before limiting it.
Offerings of lesser holiness, which may be slaughtered anywhere in the courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: Slaughter in the south ruins קדשי קדשים, but it is still a real sacrificial slaughter, because it is valid for קדשים קלים. So מעילה stays, unlike an animal that died.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key line: a flawed but real sacrificial act keeps the animal's holy status for מעילה. A complete lack of any valid act, like death, does not.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
Sacrificial animals that died are not fit at all.
But the south:
granted that it is not fit for offerings of the most sacred order,
but it is fit for offerings of lesser sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken idea of step 10 and finishes the answer to step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughter in the south is a valid type of slaughter, because it works for קדשים קלים, so it is not like death.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south keep their מעילה status, because the slaughter, though wrong for them, is still real sacrificial slaughter.

steps.title: Why list so many cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to teach all of its improper-service cases, when one would seem to be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to list all these cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's long list of cases. This sets up a detailed answer explaining why each one is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the cases teach the same rule: the animal is still subject to מעילה even though the service went wrong. So it looks like one case should have been enough to teach that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it to teach? This challenges a text that seems to say too much.
All of these cases
Offerings of the highest holiness, which must be slaughtered in the north of the courtyard

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach all of these?
phrases.notes: "All of these" means the משנה's cases: south/north, north/south, night/day, and day/night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with the first case of the משנה, the גמרא now questions the whole list of cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of several improper-service cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They all teach the same rule, so listing them all seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The two place cases each need to be taught
steps.stepSummary: Slaughter in the south with collection in the north might keep מעילה only because the collection was proper. So the reverse case had to be taught too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed. If the משנה had taught only 'slaughtered in the south and collected the blood in the north,' I would say מעילה applies there because the collection was in the north. But if he slaughtered in the north and collected in the south, the collection was in the wrong place, so I would think it leaves מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: each case is needed. It starts with the two cases about the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלה (collecting the blood) is treated as a more important act than slaughter. If only the first case were taught, we might think the proper collection in the north is what saved the מעילה. So the משנה also teaches the reverse: even when the collection was in the south, מעילה still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed. Each case teaches something the others don't.
Collecting the animal's blood in a vessel after slaughter
North / south side of the עזרה; קדשי קדשים require the north
It leaves the status of being subject to מעילה

phrases.english: They are needed:
If it had taught 'he slaughtered them in the south'
and collected their blood in the north,
here, where they are subject to מעילה,
it is because the collection was in the north.
But if he slaughtered them in the north
and collected their blood in the south,
since he collected in the south,
it would leave the status of מעילה.
phrases.notes: This is only what we would have thought. The משנה teaches this case to show it really does not leave מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by showing the first two cases are each needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case blocks a different mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only proper collection in the north keeps מעילה. Collection in the south would cancel it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even collection in the south does not remove מעילה.

steps.title: Why the night-slaughter case is needed
steps.stepSummary: The place cases happened in the daytime. Slaughter at night might be worse, because night is not a time for offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only these place cases, I would say: daytime is the time for offering, so מעילה stays. But if he slaughtered at night and sprinkled by day, night is not a time for offering. So this one who slaughtered at night would leave מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer. It shows why the case of slaughtering at night had to be added to the place cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the place cases, at least the time was right. A night slaughter is a mistake in time, and we might think that is a bigger problem. So the משנה tells us that even night slaughter keeps מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. This is the mistaken assumption the case comes to correct.
The proper time for offering, which is the daytime
Daytime

phrases.english: And if it had taught only this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the two place cases from the step before.

phrases.english: I would have said:
daytime is the time for offering,
but if he slaughtered it at night and sprinkled by day,
night is not a time for offering,
and this one, where he slaughtered at night,
would leave the status of מעילה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא, moving from mistakes in place to mistakes in time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mistake in place is minor because it happened by day. Slaughter at night, outside offering time, would cancel מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even slaughter at night keeps מעילה.

steps.title: Why sprinkling at night also needs to be taught
steps.stepSummary: Night slaughter might keep מעילה because the blood was handled by day. But sprinkling at night ruins the main act, so it might seem like strangling. The משנה teaches that it still keeps מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only 'he slaughtered it at night,' I would say: since he collected its blood by day, it is subject to מעילה. But if he slaughtered by day and sprinkled the blood at night, that is not a time for offering. Then it would be like strangled animals and not subject to מעילה. So the משנה teaches us this case too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer with the last case: day slaughter and night sprinkling. It ends with 'קמשמע לן', meaning the משנה needed to teach every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זריקה (sprinkling the blood) is the main act of the offering. So doing it at night might seem to make the whole slaughter worthless, as if the animal were strangled. An animal that died that way would lose מעילה, like קדשים שמתו in step 10. The משנה teaches that even this case keeps מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the main act of the offering
It is as if they were strangled, meaning not a real slaughter at all
It teaches us. This shows why the text was needed.

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the four cases in the משנה blocks a different mistaken idea: wrong place for slaughter, wrong place for collection, slaughter at night, and sprinkling at night. In all of them, the animal is still subject to מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This follows the same idea as steps 10-11. A slaughter that is improper is still a real slaughter, not like a dead or strangled animal, so the holiness and מעילה remain.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only 'he slaughtered it at night,'
I would have said:
since he collected its blood by day,
it is subject to מעילה,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁחָטָן בַּיּוֹם וְזָרַק דָּמָן בַּלַּיְלָה,
phrases.english: but if he slaughtered them by day and sprinkled their blood at night,
since it is not a time for offering,
it is as if they were strangled,
and they are not subject to מעילה,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תְּנָא שְׁחָטָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא with the last case and ends the answer to the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling at night ruins the main act, so it is like strangling and cancels מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even day slaughter with night sprinkling keeps מעילה, so every case in the משנה is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All four cases in the משנה are needed. Each one shows that a different kind of improper service still does not remove מעילה.

steps.title: What are wrong-intent animals still good for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of slaughter with intent outside the time or place. It asks what such an animal is fit for, since it cannot be eaten or offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one slaughtered with intent to eat or sprinkle 'outside its time' or 'outside its place,' there is still מעילה. The גמרא asks: what are these animals fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another case from the משנה and challenges it. These animals seem useless, so how can they still carry מעילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, slaughter in the south was saved because the south is still fit for קדשים קלים. A wrong intent like חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו ruins every kind of offering, even קדשים קלים. So the reason from step 11 does not work here, and these animals seem fit for nothing, just like an animal that died.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'outside its time.' Intent to eat or sprinkle after the allowed time, which makes the offering פִּיגּוּל.
Literally 'outside its place.' Intent to eat or sprinkle outside the allowed area, which makes the offering פָּסוּל.
For what are they fit? A challenge that asks what use something still has.

steps.confusionAlert: The animal was not actually taken outside its time or place. The problem is only what the person intended while slaughtering it.

phrases.english: Outside its time and outside its place.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. It means slaughtering with the intent to eat or sprinkle at the wrong time or in the wrong place.

phrases.english: For what are they fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case in the משנה. It uses the 'fit for nothing' reasoning from Step 11 to challenge the ruling of מעילה here.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that מעילה applies to animals slaughtered with intent חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The south case kept מעילה because the south is fit for קדשים קלים. Wrong intent disqualifies every offering, even קדשים קלים, so these animals are fit for nothing, like קדשים שמתו, and should have no מעילה.

steps.title: The blood still works to make it פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sprinkling of the blood still 'works' for these offerings, at least to give them the status of פיגול. So they are still real קדשים and carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the sprinkling still makes them 'accepted' for their פיגול status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. These animals are still useful in one way: the blood service still takes effect on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering only becomes true פיגול if its blood is sprinkled on the altar the proper way. So the sprinkling still has a real effect on this animal, even if that effect is to make it פיגול. Because the altar service still 'counts' for it, the animal has not lost its holiness, and מעילה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because. Introduces the reason.
They make it 'accepted.' Here this is the effect of the blood sprinkling on the altar.
An offering made unfit because of intent to eat or sprinkle it after its proper time. Eating it carries כָּרֵת.

steps.whatToRemember: The dead animal is fit for nothing, so it has no מעילה. An offering slaughtered with the wrong intent is different, because the blood service still takes effect on it, even if only to make it פיגול. So it keeps its holiness and its מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that keeps returning in this סוגיא: מעילה stays as long as the קרבן's service still 'works' on some level, even for a bad result.

phrases.english: Since they are made accepted for their פיגול status.
phrases.notes: Something only becomes real פיגול if its blood was sprinkled properly. So the sprinkling still counts for this animal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case is not 'fit for nothing,' because the altar service still takes effect on it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These animals are useless like the dead animal, so they should have no מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood sprinkling still takes effect and gives them פיגול status. So they are still holy and carry מעילה.
